findings.title: Public article policy discloses every unpublished draft
findings.category: Broken Access Control / Confidential Data Exposure
findings.rationale:
The browser uses the public anon client created at src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13 to select article rows at src/components/ArticleList.tsx:37-52, establishing an externally reachable read path. RLS is enabled, but the SELECT policy at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:68-69 applies an unconditional USING (true), with no published or author restriction; the home page’s client-side published filter at src/components/ArticleList.tsx:48-50 does not protect direct API access. The unauthenticated article route also fetches all fields by attacker-supplied ID without checking publication status at src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:27-47 and src/App.tsx:113-117, confirming there is no authentication or authorization gate protecting draft content.

The public anonymous client in `src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13` can read article rows, while the RLS policy at `supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:68-69` unconditionally permits every SELECT. The published-only condition in `src/components/ArticleList.tsx:48-50` is client-side, and `src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:27-47` reads all fields without a publication or authentication check, so remote unauthenticated disclosure of any stored draft is realistic.

findings.title: Tautological RLS policy allows anonymous editing and reassignment of every article
findings.rationale:
The shipped client performs an articles UPDATE at src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:61, while src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13 configures the browser client with the public anon key, so the Supabase API is an externally reachable untrusted boundary. The policy at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:76-78 has no role restriction and uses an exhaustive null tautology, authorizing every existing row and, through the implicit check, every resulting row. The ownership comparison at src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:21 only controls whether buttons render at src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:240 and supplies no database-side authorization against a direct client/API update.

The UPDATE policy at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:76-78 applies without a role restriction and its tautological USING expression authorizes every article row, with the same condition implicitly governing resulting rows. The public browser client at src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13 reaches this boundary with the anon key, while src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:21 and :240 only hide UI controls and do not enforce database authorization for the update at :61.

findings.title: Tautological RLS policy permits unauthenticated modification of any profile
findings.rationale:
The browser creates its Supabase client with the public anon key at src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13, and the application reaches the profiles update operation at src/components/Profile.tsx:45. Although RLS is enabled at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:20, the UPDATE policy at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:53-55 has no role restriction and uses a tautology without an ownership check or separate WITH CHECK. The UI passes the current user's ID at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:64, but that client-side restriction does not protect the externally reachable Data API, allowing an anon or authenticated caller to modify another row's writable profile fields.

The public client uses the anon key at src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13, while the profiles SELECT policy at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:43-45 exposes rows needed to identify a target. The UPDATE policy at lines 53-55 applies without a role restriction and authorizes every row through a tautology, so the client-side user-ID constraint in src/components/Profile.tsx:45-51 does not prevent unauthenticated remote modification through a deployed Data API.

findings.title: Tautological DELETE policy lets anonymous callers erase users and their articles
findings.rationale:
Assuming the standard externally reachable Supabase/PostgREST boundary, anonymous callers are untrusted and use the browser-exposed anon client configured at src/lib/supabase.ts:13. The DELETE policy defaults to PUBLIC and has a tautological USING clause at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:58, while the public SELECT policy at line 43 exposes victim identifiers. Deleting a profile triggers the explicit ON DELETE CASCADE on articles.author_id at line 30, so the impact is feasible cross-user data destruction.

The DELETE policy at `supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:58` has no role restriction and its tautological `USING` expression permits anonymous deletion of any profile exposed by the public SELECT policy at line 43. The browser client uses the public anon credentials at `src/lib/supabase.ts:13`, and deleting a victim profile cascades to that user’s articles through the foreign key at line 30, enabling unauthenticated cross-user data destruction.

findings.title: Public RLS policy exposes every user's email address
findings.category: Broken Access Control / Sensitive Data Exposure
findings.rationale:
The shipped browser client uses the public anon configuration at src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13, and src/components/Profile.tsx:23-27 confirms direct client-side `profiles` reads with `select('*')`. The table stores email with each profile at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:11-16, while its SELECT policy omits a role restriction and unconditionally permits every row at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:43-45. The UI’s authenticated dashboard gate at src/App.tsx:118-123 does not constrain direct requests to the externally reachable Supabase API, and no repository grant restriction or narrower SELECT policy protects anon callers.

The browser client exposes the public Supabase configuration at src/lib/supabase.ts:6-13, while the profiles SELECT policy unconditionally permits every row at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:43-45. Because profiles include email at migration lines 11-16 and the client directly selects all profile fields at src/components/Profile.tsx:23-27, an unauthenticated remote caller can access sensitive profile data without an additional exploitation precondition; the dashboard gate at src/App.tsx:118-123 does not protect the API.

findings.title: Tautological RLS policy permits anonymous deletion of all articles
findings.rationale:
The shipped delete call begins at src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:80 and applies the route-derived article ID at src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:83; its author check at src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:240 only hides the client button. The browser uses the public anon client at src/lib/supabase.ts:4-13, while supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:81-83 defines a PUBLIC DELETE policy whose condition is tautologically true, with no authentication or ownership constraint. Assuming the documented standard Supabase deployment at README.md:39-55 and its default public-table grants, an anonymous caller can delete arbitrary article rows, and no protective REVOKE or narrower policy exists in the repository.

Assuming the documented standard Supabase deployment and unchanged default public-table grants, the public anon client in src/lib/supabase.ts:4-13 can reach the destructive operation without authentication. The DELETE policy at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:81-83 has a tautological condition and no ownership check, while the author check around src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:240 only hides the UI control and does not protect the database operation at lines 80-83.

findings.title: Article ownership is enforced only by hidden UI controls
preconditions: A valid authenticated user account and session.
Knowledge of an article UUID belonging to another user, exposed through the public article listing and route.
findings.rationale:
The externally reachable `/article/:id` route supplies attacker-controlled `id` to `ArticlePage` (src/App.tsx:114, src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:10), and the save and delete handlers mutate by that ID alone (src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:61, src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:80). `isAuthor` only controls rendered buttons (src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:21, src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:240), while the deployed UPDATE and DELETE RLS predicates are tautologies with no `auth.uid() = author_id` ownership check (supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:76, supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:81). Assuming the public route and browser Supabase client cross an untrusted-user boundary, an authenticated user can modify or delete another author's row, causing feasible integrity and data-loss impact.

`ArticlePage` takes the route-controlled ID and uses it alone for updates and deletes at `src/pages/ArticlePage.tsx:61-64` and `:80-83`; the ownership check at line 21 only hides controls at line 240. Assuming the deployed backend uses the checked-in migration, its tautological UPDATE and DELETE policies at `supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:76-83` provide no server-side owner check. Two realistic preconditions and authenticated access both derive MEDIUM, so the scanner’s HIGH rating is overstated by one band.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Yoan Bernabeu (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Stored avatar URLs make visitors' browsers request attacker-chosen hosts
preconditions: Attacker has an authenticated account with a profile and published article visible in the public feed.
A visitor loads the affected feed while their browser can reach the attacker-controlled HTTPS image host.
findings.rationale:
Authenticated users reach the profile editor through `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:64`; browser-controlled input at `src/components/Profile.tsx:162`–`165` is persisted unchanged by `handleSave` at `src/components/Profile.tsx:45`–`51` and rendered as an image URL at `src/components/Profile.tsx:117`. The same stored value reaches unauthenticated visitors through the public home feed (`src/pages/Home.tsx:15`, `src/components/ArticleList.tsx:100`–`103`), while the database permits public profile reads at `supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:42`–`45`. No origin or scheme restriction covers the path; `type="url"` does not constrain destination hosts, so an attacker-controlled HTTPS image host can receive visitor requests and metadata even where browser policy blocks some private-network or mixed-content destinations.

`Profile.tsx:45`–`51` persists the user-controlled avatar URL without origin restriction, and `ArticleList.tsx:100`–`103` renders it for public-feed visitors under the public-read policy at migration lines 42–45. This permits an authenticated attacker’s image host to receive visitor requests and associated metadata; no named deployed control mitigates the path.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Yoan Bernabeu (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Public SECURITY DEFINER RPC exposes a caller-unscoped email lookup oracle
preconditions: The migration is deployed on an externally reachable RPC path with PUBLIC/anonymous execution unchanged.
A profile exists for an email address the caller can supply or guess.
findings.rationale:
The migration creates an externally callable function taking caller-controlled email text and marks it `SECURITY DEFINER` at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:90-94. Its only predicate compares the supplied email directly and returns identifiers and email data, with no `auth.uid()`, JWT-claim, or role check at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:95-100. The permissive profile policy at supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:42-45 does not protect this path and instead confirms that anonymous callers currently face no data-access gate; under the measurement exception, the intentional-vulnerability labels do not exclude it.

The `SECURITY DEFINER` function at lines 90-100 accepts caller-controlled email text and returns profile identifiers and email data without an identity or role check. The migration shows no execution restriction, while the policy at lines 42-45 also supplies no protective data-access gate. With two preconditions but unauthenticated remote access, the required lower-result rule yields MEDIUM, making the claimed HIGH one tier too severe.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Yoan Bernabeu (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Article listing silently truncates as the table grows
findings.rationale: The public route renders `ArticleList` through `src/pages/Home.tsx:15`, and `src/components/ArticleList.tsx:37-52` does omit explicit pagination while refetching after Realtime events at `src/components/ArticleList.tsx:23-25`. However, visitors cannot control the query shape, and growing the table requires authenticated inserts constrained by `supabase/migrations/20250201000000_initial_vulnblog.sql:72-73`; the claimed security effect therefore depends on request/row volume and falls under the volumetric-DoS exclusion.
